newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent firms, cold weather in U.S. supports.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent firms, cold weather in U.S. supports.

text.p: Brent crude futures prices were firmer in late afternoon dealings on Thursday, supported by overnight news on Iraq and the U.S. weather.
March Brent was last traded on SIMEX at $22.81 per barrel, up four cents from London's overnight settlement. April was up four cents at $22.34.
A broker said he expected London to test $23.00 on March later in the day.
NYMEX March crude was last traded at $24.49 per barrel, up two cents from the New York close and just two cents above the intraday low.
Brokers said the Brent market remained technically supported after the recent failure of the front-month to break $22.00.

In addition, Weather Services Corp said colder-than-normal temperatures would prevail in the U.S. northeast in its 6-10 day forecast and news of a potential power struggle in Baghdad were also supporting the market, brokers said.
The cold weather forecasts supported NYMEX heating oil overnight. February was last traded at 69.05 cents per gallon, up 0.21 from New York.
